title: Same Verdict, Different Reasons: LLM-as-a-Judge and Clinician Disagreement on Medical Chatbot Completeness

live_model.evidence: "We evaluated three backbone LLM Judges: Llama 3.3-70B, OpenBioLLM-70B, and GPT-5 Mini (gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07)" (Sec. 3.1); "GPT-5 Mini was run at the default temperature of 1.0".

prompt.location: Table 9 (Analytical-Rubric grading prompt), Tables 7-8, 10 (General-Likert and FSS variants), Tables 4-6 (Dynamic-Checklist)
prompt.note: Full grading prompts printed in Appendix D tables; structured JSON output, max 4,096 tokens.

claim.metric: F1 for the Incomplete class vs clinician ground truth (HealthBench, Analytical-Rubric)
claim.location: Table 1, HealthBench block, row Analytical-Rubric, GPT-5 Mini columns (F1 0.76, Prec 0.86, Rec 0.68, AUC 0.66)

data.source: HealthBench (Arora et al., 2025), filtered to 1,281 single-turn English conversations with fine-grained rubric and ideal answer (Sec. 3.2, App. B.2); MedExpert (108 questions) also used

notes: Ground truth is not a released label: it is built by grading each HealthBench ideal answer against its clinician-written positive rubric criteria with GPT-4.1 (75% threshold), so re-execution needs one GPT-4.1 pass plus the GPT-5 Mini judge pass. gpt-4-turbo in live_ids is only a citation of prior work (Sec. 2). Default temperature 1.0 adds variance.
